newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl says "I know my duty" on fresh candidacy.
newsitem.headline: Kohl says "I know my duty" on fresh candidacy.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, who has declined to commit himself to standing again in the 1998 general election, told a meeting of his party on Tuesday that he "knew his duty", participants said.

Kohl told the Christian Democrat members of parliament that he would not let anyone force him into making a decision before he was ready. But then he said he knew he had a responsibility to the party and the coalition, adding: "I know my duty."
Deputies greeted the remark with a long round of applause.

Kohl has come under pressure to give his party and the coalition government, divided over major reforms to the tax and pensions systems and struggling to stem high unemployment, fresh impetus by saying he will stand again in October 1998.

But Kohl, Europe's longest serving head of government, has so far declined to commit himself. In an interview 10 days ago on French television, he said he would ponder the matter after a European Union reform summit in June.
